title: The lad who brought the water
summary: The knapper's son of Dùn ìseal is sent to the hill's crown with water for the man who has just taken it unopposed, and is asked his name and whether the spear he carries is his father's best. Told to take it home and to tell his father the king will want a great many more.

title: The valleys come in to the hill
summary: Through the first year the households of the valleys about Dùn ìseal come in to the king one after another, unsummoned, bringing hides, pots, and whatever else they judge fitting, and with their gifts their grazing and their old quarrels, for a telling to be held over them.

title: The first judgement on the hill
summary: Two households of Dùn ìseal bring before the king a strip of pasture each has claimed for a generation. He asks one question, of whose cattle grazed it before the boundary stone was last moved, and gives the strip back in a sentence. Neither household ever brings the matter before him again.

title: The king's order to the flint-pit
summary: The flint-pit behind the houses of Dùn ìseal is set, on the king's own word, to cut spearheads by the score rather than as they are needed, the first order of its kind on the hill. The knapper's son is set to the work alongside his father before that year's leaves are down.

title: The warmth with no fire
summary: In the first hard winter on the hill, a girl of Dùn ìseal stands near the king's own untended fire at night and finds herself warmed through though no flame burns close enough to account for it. She keeps the telling to herself for years before it is believed.

title: The line of the bank pegged in the snow
summary: In the depth of the same winter the king walks the crown of Dùn ìseal setting ash pegs with his own hand, marking a line that takes in the old byres and ground for houses not yet built. The households break the frozen turf along it through the worst of the frost.

title: Flint tools finish the bank's ditch
summary: When the antler mattocks digging the new ditch at Dùn ìseal blunt faster than they can be sharpened in the frost, the flint-pit sends up scrapers of worked stone to finish the work, so that the hill's first bank is cut as much with flint as with iron.

title: Muireall and Gormshuil brought to the hill
summary: As the frost breaks a small company comes down from the high valleys to Dùn ìseal: Muireall, the king's wife, and Gormshuil, his young daughter, with a few kin and hands beside them. The hill, which had thought the king had no household of his own, falls quiet to let them through the new gate.

title: Dòmhnall born within the new bank
summary: A son is born to Muireall inside the finished bank of Dùn ìseal, the first of the king's children to draw breath on ground he holds, and the hill takes it as a settled thing that the king has come to stay among them.

title: A spearhead given for nothing
summary: The knapper cuts a spearhead finer than any he has made that year, for no order and no payment, and sends it up to the king's fire on the birth of the king's son. He will not say why, only that the giving seemed owed.
